newsitem.title: UK: Freeze lifts NWE gas oil premiums, diesel revives.
newsitem.headline: Freeze lifts NWE gas oil premiums, diesel revives.

text.p: Frigid weather and frozen waterways around northern Europe helped lift gas oil premiums by around $1 a tonne in busy post-holiday volumes on Thursday, traders said.

Good buying interest boosted German winter grade heating oil cargoes bids to around Feb +$8.50/10 cif NWE for mid-month and around Feb IPE +$8.50/9 for end-month. Low sulphur diesel demand continued to revive, with product trading about $1 firmer.
Jan IPE gas oil closed $3.50 firmer at $234 a tonne and Feb IPE gained +$4.75 to $231 on the freeze and similar weather forecast for the United States by the end of the week.
French low sulphur diesel traded at Feb IPE +$13 cif NWE.
That was for loading January 23-28 and at fob quotes high +$2 into Milford Haven. A cargo of Algerian gas oil traded into La Pallice at Feb IPE +$12.
Cargoes of 10,00-15,000 tonnes of Russian heating oil were offered around $1 firmer at mean quotes +$2 cif Rotterdam. German winter grade

In barges, prompt refinery grade heating oil traded most frequently at Jan IPE +$4. January 13-20 barges were done at Jan IPE +$3.50 and January 20-30 traded at Jan IPE +$2.50. Bulls also found support from ice problems near Rotterdam.
